tasks.short: Distribute released production schedules and work orders, then resolve missing acknowledgements.

steps.what: Retrieve the released production schedule and associated work orders.
Check schedule versions, department assignments and release status.
Prepare separate schedule documents for each department.
Send schedule packets and highlight changes to department supervisors.
Chase missing acknowledgements and resolve access or routing problems.

tasks.design: Configure release events in the {OPS_SYSTEM} to publish department views and revision differences through {WORKFLOW}. Send links through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}, track acknowledgements and route overdue or failed deliveries to the clerk; generate controlled printouts only where needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Department copies drifted from the released schedule. Routing lists and acknowledgements lived outside the production record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release events, permissions and notification rules can handle most distribution. AI-assisted coding makes missing connectors and revision comparisons cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Shared terminals, offline workstations and obsolete printed copies still need practical controls.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an acknowledgement hides a misunderstanding about what the department must actually change.
tasks.altitude: The clerk checks distribution exceptions instead of assembling daily packets. With delegated authority, they can correct routing and access within agreed limits; production priorities remain with production management.

reach.task: Prepare dispatch work from the latest released production schedule.
reach.learn: Understand dispatch cutoffs, order identifiers and which schedule changes affect loading.

evidence.claim: Release-triggered routing, revision comparison and acknowledgement reminders can use configured workflows without a model.
Boltrics provides operational records across warehouse and transport functions; this does not establish production schedule distribution capability.

assumptions: A released schedule has a stable identifier and revision.
Digital department views can replace most separately prepared packets.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Production execution uses order-to-cash because the workflow list has no production-specific stream.
Build ranges assume one site and existing system licences.
unknowns: Whether release events, department permissions and acknowledgement features are available.
Which departments require controlled paper copies.
Who may change routing and distribution rules.
Whether acknowledgement logging requires employee consultation under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Can existing release subscriptions meet the need before building a connector?
What evidence distinguishes delivery, acknowledgement and operational acceptance?
new_work: Resolve failed deliveries and incorrect access.
Maintain department routing and escalation rules.
Check that obsolete printed schedules are withdrawn.
Apply GDPR access and retention controls where acknowledgement records identify employees.

tasks.short: Revise production schedules after disruptions and agree the resulting tradeoffs.

steps.what: Check shortages, backlog, capacity and current production progress.
Read engineering changes and interruption notes for scheduling implications.

loop.input: Approved engineering changes and interruption notes linked to work orders.
loop.output: Proposed dates, affected items, dependencies and constraints, each with a source passage.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units, approval status and dates; the clerk confirms extracted constraints before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved or conflicting fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured changes use direct fields, but free-text notes contain constraints that fixed mappings miss.

steps.what: Calculate alternative sequences and their effects on completion dates.
Discuss feasible changes with production, engineering and sales.
Choose and approve a revised schedule within operational and commercial limits.
Enter the approved revision and release the updated production schedule.

tasks.design: Join current production and material data from {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, then run a deterministic scheduling solver on {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop turns free-text changes in {DOCS} into checked constraints, while {WORKFLOW} presents alternatives for discussion and approval before releasing the selected revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local constraints were incomplete, and spreadsheet scenarios took too long to rebuild during interruptions. Several departments controlled different parts of the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Established scheduling solvers and system interfaces already address the calculation. AI-assisted coding reduces connector work, while bounded extraction helps with approved free-text changes.
tasks.still_hard: Setup times, uncertain recovery dates and conflicting customer commitments can defeat an apparently feasible schedule. Agreement between departments remains necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Judge which promise to protect, negotiate scarce capacity and recognise operational constraints missing from the data.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time comparing recovery options with supervisors and less time rebuilding scenarios. Delegated limits could let them release small resequencing changes; production management retains decisions affecting major commitments or extra spending.

reach.task: Balance recovery options across material availability, capacity and customer commitments.
reach.learn: Learn constraint modelling, scenario sensitivity and the authority limits for changing commitments.

reach.task: Assess how production revisions affect dispatch capacity.
reach.learn: Learn transport cutoffs and how to distinguish forecast dates from confirmed promises.

evidence.claim: Constraint solvers can calculate production alternatives; local feasibility and commercial tradeoffs still require validation.
Qargo documents PDF order extraction, supporting bounded document intake as an existing capability, not production constraint interpretation.
The EU AI Act identifies certain employment-related allocation and monitoring uses; scope depends on the actual scheduling design.

assumptions: The initial scope schedules work orders and aggregate capacity, without scoring individual workers.
A solver first uses existing planning capability where it can express the required constraints.
Every released revision refers to the exact approved scenario and data snapshot.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one site, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to employee data; national rules determine consultation requirements. Consultation lead times can exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Whether existing planning configuration can represent setup, material and capacity constraints.
Which decisions the clerk can make without management approval.
Whether staffing data contains identifiable employee information.
Whether the intended allocation or monitoring features fall within EU AI Act employment provisions.
Which employee consultation and working-time requirements apply under national rules.
research_questions: Which historical disruptions expose missing constraints in the current schedule?
Can the current planning configuration solve representative cases before commissioning a separate solver?
Which changes require commercial approval as well as production approval?
new_work: Maintain setup times, priorities and solver constraints.
Review extracted constraints and resolve conflicting source notes.
Investigate infeasible scenarios and stale production events.
Monitor scenario stability so frequent recalculation does not cause constant resequencing.
Maintain approval limits, access controls and the applicable consultation arrangements.

tasks.short: Determine material and capacity requirements from work orders, schedules and staffing information.

steps.what: Retrieve current work orders, production schedules and staffing tables.
Read work-order attachments and approved notes for additional requirements.

loop.input: Approved work-order attachments and notes without structured requirement fields.
loop.output: Item quantities, setup needs, skill categories and due dates with source passages.
loop.check: Check revision, item identifiers, units and quantities against master data; confirm additions before calculation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per attachment; unreadable, contradictory or unknown requirements go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use direct mappings for structured fields; varying free-text instructions need bounded interpretation.

steps.what: Calculate material quantities and capacity requirements across scheduled work.
Compare requirements with usable inventory, reservations and available capacity.
Confirm material priorities and resolve unusual capacity requirements with the supervisor.

tasks.design: Configure requirements calculation and availability checks in {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, using approved bills of materials and routing standards. Use a bounded loop only for unstructured attachments in {DOCS}, then show shortages and aggregate capacity gaps in {BI} for supervisor decisions on exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were split between master data, attachments and local calculations. Missing revisions and uncertain stock availability made automatic results hard to trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing requirements planning handles structured calculations. Cheaper integration development and source-linked extraction can cover the remaining document gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect bills of materials, quarantined stock, undocumented substitutions and unrealistic routing standards still produce misleading answers.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unusual setups and distinguish a genuine shortage from stock that is recorded but unusable.
tasks.altitude: The clerk investigates requirement exceptions and discusses readiness before each shift. With delegated limits, they can resolve approved master-data discrepancies; supervisors retain substitution and staffing decisions.

reach.task: Reconcile usable stock and reservations against production demand.
reach.learn: Learn stock status, lot restrictions and reservation rules.

reach.task: Determine whether held materials can enter production.
reach.learn: Learn release evidence, traceability requirements and why availability differs from physical quantity.

evidence.claim: Bills of materials, routing standards and availability rules support deterministic requirement calculations when master data is maintained.
Qargo documents extraction from PDF orders; applying extraction to manufacturing requirements still needs local validation.

assumptions: Requirements are mostly structured; attachments carry a smaller set of additional constraints.
This differs from the document-heavy prior because standard production orders commonly reference master data.
Staffing inputs use aggregate availability and skill categories where possible.
Outputs do not rank employees or allocate named people.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one site.
unknowns: How much requirement information exists only in attachments.
Whether bills of materials and routing standards match current production.
Whether stock statuses and reservations are reliable.
Whether aggregate staffing availability is sufficient.
Which access and consultation requirements apply under GDPR and national rules.
research_questions: Which requirement fields cause the most corrections today?
Can attachment requirements become structured fields at their source?
Which shortage rules already exist in the current planning configuration?
new_work: Review uncertain extractions and missing source revisions.
Correct master-data exceptions through the approved change process.
Maintain stock-status and capacity interpretation rules.
Check that aggregated staffing data remains sufficient and appropriately restricted.

tasks.short: Arrange parts delivery and internal handling to keep production moving.

steps.what: Check shortages, part locations and required delivery times.
Request current availability and delivery promises from existing suppliers.
Negotiate practical delivery or assembly arrangements with suppliers and department supervisors.
Approve premium freight or other commitments outside the clerk's authority.
Book the agreed delivery and confirm the collection or arrival slot.
Create internal movement or assembly orders against the released production schedule.
Agree safe handling and assembly sequence with the warehouse and production teams.
Verify delivered parts against the delivery booking and movement order.
Record receipt and update the expedite status for production planning.

tasks.design: Connect shortages in {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to an expedite record in {WORKFLOW}, with standard availability enquiries through {EMAIL}. Prepare bookings through {PARTNER_PORTAL} for clerk approval, generate internal orders from approved arrangements and update status from confirmed receipt events.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier promises, bookings and internal handling instructions were disconnected. Staff had to chase each handoff without a shared exception record.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured enquiries, approval rules and event links can remove much of the chase. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of supplier mappings and duplicate-booking checks; no model is needed for the proposed core flow.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier promises can change, some portals lack interfaces, and physical handling depends on local capacity and safe working arrangements.
tasks.human_edge: Secure credible commitments, negotiate recovery options and coordinate people when the planned movement cannot happen.
tasks.altitude: The clerk concentrates on threatened commitments and recovery conversations. Delegated spending and booking limits could let them complete routine expedites independently; exceptional costs remain with the supply chain manager.

reach.task: Coordinate inbound receipts and internal movements against production priorities.
reach.learn: Learn receiving capacity, stock accuracy and safe material handoff requirements.

reach.task: Compare recovery transport options for production-critical parts.
reach.learn: Learn transport constraints, premium freight economics and how to verify a delivery promise.

evidence.claim: Standard enquiries, spending checks, booking validation and receipt-driven updates can use deterministic workflows.
A Smurfit Kappa plant case reports reduced truck turnaround after time-slot management; it supports delivery coordination, not end-to-end parts expediting.
Boltrics provides warehouse and transport records that can support connected material movements.

assumptions: The steps describe a supplier-linked expedite; internal-only cases skip supplier enquiries and external booking.
Standard enquiries request information without changing orders, prices or commitments.
Manager approval is conditional on spending or commitment thresholds.
Automated internal orders use approved work instructions and released production priorities.
Physical verification remains with receiving staff; automation records their confirmed result.
Time shares cover the participating roles in this task and are estimates, not a measured clerk-only time study.
unknowns: Which suppliers support structured promises and booking interfaces.
Which purchases and bookings fall within the clerk's authority.
How receipt confirmations reach the operational systems.
Which assembly activities need separate technical or quality approval.
Whether changed tracking or working arrangements require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which supplier interfaces cover the largest share of expedite cases?
What checks prevent duplicate bookings after a timeout or changed promise?
Which internal handoffs fail despite a confirmed external delivery?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting supplier promises.
Maintain supplier mappings, spending limits and enquiry templates.
Investigate delivery discrepancies and failed receipt updates.
Maintain access and GDPR retention controls for supplier and employee contact records.

role.altitude: The role shifts from copying schedules and chasing status toward preparing recovery choices and resolving exceptions across departments. Greater decision rights depend on explicit delegation for resequencing, bookings and spending.
reach: Support supply chain managers with costed disruption scenarios.
Work with inventory clerks on usable stock and reservation accuracy.
Help logistics analysts connect production changes to dispatch constraints.
Work with quality control managers on held-material readiness.
skills_to_grow: Model material, setup and capacity constraints.
Read scenario tradeoffs and test sensitivity to uncertain inputs.
Maintain master-data quality and traceable revisions.
Understand approval limits, GDPR and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run a short-horizon production readiness and recovery service that connects material availability, feasible schedules and delivery commitments, with delegated authority for small operational changes.
